topology: R1 backbone ASBR and R2 ABR share area0; R2 attaches R3 NSSA ASBR and R4 leaf in area10. PC2 is behind R1, PC1 behind R4. R1 external203.0.113.0/24 hosts upstream SRV1; R3 external198.51.100.0/24 hosts local SRV2. Prefix-list/route-map EXTERNAL on each ASBR redistributes only its connected external prefix at metric20. Transits cost10 and passive LANs1. Initially area10 is incorrectly stub; intended design is NSSA on R2/R3/R4 with explicit ABR Type7 default.
implemented: Twenty-third ENARSI Layer 3 Technologies entry with independent practice/reference documents, eight-row addressing and role plan, staged guide, verified IOS/Windows commands and current-origin/path/query permalinks. Existing layout, themes, artwork, terminal styling and offline single-HTML delivery are preserved.

Initial diagnosis proves four actual failed local-service directions (PC1/SRV2 and PC2/SRV2) with two working upstream PC1/SRV1 control directions. The initial stub has Full peers and an automatic summary default but cannot export the NSSA ASBR external prefix. This distinguishes connected service reachability from OSPF external advertisement.

Consistent area10 NSSA membership permits R3’s local198.51.100.0/24 Type7/N2 advertisement. R4 and R2 install N2 at AD110/metric20; R1 installs translated E2 at20 through the single ABR2.2.2.2. The ABR translator runtime, received topology and database views identify R3 as Type7 advertiser and R2 as Type5 translator. Upstream203.0.113.0 Type5 stays outside the NSSA.

Explicit area10 nssa default-information-originate on R2 supplies a Type7/O N2 default at metric1 to R3/R4 without requiring a default at R2 itself. Plain NSSA retains IA specifics. Removing just the option preserves NSSA, removes default RIB and database entries, breaks only upstream-service directions and leaves local N2 and core E2 service paths working.

Totally-NSSA comparison explicitly removes the Type7-default option before enabling no-summary on the ABR. The Type3/O IA default costs11, nondefault IA specifics disappear and local Type7/N2 plus translated E2 remain. Restoration explicitly removes no-summary before restoring the intended Type7 default.

Six observed exercises cover missing explicit default, totally-NSSA comparison, actual membership mismatch, withdrawal/recovery of R3 connected redistribution, ABR no-redistribution scope and backbone attachment loss/recovery. The ABR scope option does not suppress another ASBR’s prefix. During backbone loss, local NSSA N2 traffic remains operational while translated backbone access and upstream default access fail. Physical carrier remains up during configuration faults.

Success requires three unique original requests, accepted destinations, parent-linked replies and expected router egresses in all six directions. Failure correlates original requests with actual No route drops of requests or their replies at the expected router and excludes received success. Configuration/RIB epochs reject stale or configuration-only proof. PC2 must receive the complete translated-service HTTP response, and PC1 the upstream-default HTTP response.

Seven live checks cover policy, received neighbors, NSSA routes, backbone translation, database, service health and saved configs. Nine historical checks cover diagnosis, actual traffic, two-service HTTP and six exercises. Practice0/16, diagnosis1/16, repaired baseline10/16 and full16/16; reference seven live checks only. Portable YAML retains observed work while dropping/rebuilding runtime; new practice starts fresh.

Fixed the database display’s NSSA default classification: it previously invented a Type3 default for plain NSSA and omitted the configured Type7 default. Plain NSSA without explicit default now shows neither, configured explicit default is Type7 and never appears as translated Type5, and totally NSSA uses the summary Type3 default. The default’s Options text correctly says No Type 7/5 translation, while the local nondefault Type7 prefix remains eligible. Stub defaults remain unchanged.
scope: IOS OSPFv2 single-ABR NSSA external redistribution, plain/explicit-default/totally-NSSA comparison, logical Type7-to-Type5 translation and actual simulated control/data-plane delivery. The engine exchanges segmented logical router records; Type3/5/7 database views are projected from received records rather than individually scoped binary LSAs. No fresh CML capture, binary E/N/P-bit interoperability, full forwarding-address resolution rules, multiple-ABR election/grace-period FSM, translator policy commands or complete RFC timing/flooding conformance is claimed.
